feedback.trigger: A task encounters project-owned contracts or a subset skill install.
feedback.actual_behavior: The router replaces project rules or silently invents missing defaults.
feedback.expected_behavior: Project authority wins; missing defaults affect dependent work only.
feedback.invariant: Optional plans preserve existing SOW routing, project authority, and evidence-backed acceptance.

scenarios.request: Draft a requested plan.
scenarios.context: The target project declares its own active plan and SOW templates.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use the project contracts and planning paths, not AISkills defaults.
scenarios.must_not: Override project authority or require a new SOW merely for plan creation.

scenarios.request: Fix wording in a document.
scenarios.context: Repo guardrails permit docs-only edits; no plan is required.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use the existing docs-only/no-SOW branch and leave plan-specific gates inactive.
scenarios.must_not: Force SOW or plan creation.

scenarios.request: Draft a plan from an installed review skill.
scenarios.context: No project contract, supplied contract, or router owner is available.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Identify missing contract and leave dependent drafting unverified; unrelated work remains allowed.
scenarios.must_not: Invent a template, assume sibling roots, or auto-install the owner.

feedback.trigger: A task needs routing before choosing a plan.
feedback.actual_behavior: Coordinated or multi-file work automatically gets a plan.
feedback.expected_behavior: Preserve SOW routing; create a plan only by explicit request or excessive-scope risk.
feedback.invariant: Optional plans preserve existing SOW routing, project authority, and evidence-backed acceptance.

scenarios.request: Create a plan for this bounded task.
scenarios.context: The user explicitly requests a plan; SOW policy is unchanged.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use the canonical contract and map original goal to G# and acceptance; do not infer implementation approval.
scenarios.must_not: Treat plan approval as SOW approval.

scenarios.request: Implement an ordinary change across multiple files and owners.
scenarios.context: An approved SOW covers the exact task; no excessive-scope risk or plan request exists.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Reuse approved coverage without a new SOW or plan; preserve existing routing.
scenarios.must_not: Create a plan from file count, owners, or dependencies alone.

scenarios.request: Organize this extremely large change safely.
scenarios.context: Completing the scope in one SOW risks non-completion or mistakes.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Create a compact plan and bounded SOW sequence; keep proposed work separate from approved scope.
scenarios.must_not: Treat TBD SOWs or status markers as permission to implement.

feedback.trigger: A request needs a new architecture-affecting SOW.
feedback.actual_behavior: The router drafts an implementation direction before reading project authority documents.
feedback.expected_behavior: Audit project authority before branch selection or SOW direction and stop on unresolved conflict.
feedback.invariant: Routing derives design constraints from the target project's authority documents.

scenarios.request: Draft a migration that changes persistence ownership.
scenarios.context: The project design document defines a persistence ownership invariant.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Read the authority, map viable directions to it, and draft only a compliant SOW direction.
scenarios.must_not: Route directly to a convenience-driven implementation plan.

scenarios.request: Correct a typo in a planning document.
scenarios.context: No architecture, ownership, or runtime contract is affected.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use the docs-only branch without requiring a design audit.
scenarios.must_not: Create architectural work from an editorial request.

scenarios.request: Draft a redesign where the authority documents are silent on the proposed ownership split.
scenarios.context: The change would establish a new architecture contract.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Stop and request a project-authority decision before drafting the implementation direction.
scenarios.must_not: Treat silence as approval.

feedback.trigger: A SOW or extension is created, approved, reopened, or finished.
feedback.actual_behavior: Lifecycle times are omitted or recorded as date-only values while redundant approval evidence may be added.
feedback.expected_behavior: Record concise approval metadata plus create, approve, and finish datetimes with clock time and timezone for the SOW and every extension.
feedback.invariant: SOW lifecycle is explicit, uses full timezone-aware datetimes, and is free of transcript-style approval evidence.

scenarios.request: Create a SOW, record my approval, then close it after implementation.
scenarios.context: The exact lifecycle transition times are known.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Record create_dttm, approve_dttm, and finish_dttm at their respective transitions as full datetimes such as 2026-09-11T15:42:07+07:00, with a concise approval marker.
scenarios.must_not: Use a date-only timestamp, add approval transcript, message identifiers, quoted evidence, or an Approval-Evidence field.

scenarios.request: Review this draft SOW but do not approve it.
scenarios.context: The SOW exists, but no approval or completion occurred.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Keep approve_dttm and finish_dttm null while preserving create_dttm as a full datetime with time and timezone.
scenarios.must_not: Infer approval from review, write future timestamps, or reduce create_dttm to a date-only value.

scenarios.request: Add an extension to an older SOW whose original exact timestamps are unavailable.
scenarios.context: The new extension times are known, while historical SOW times are not authoritative.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use unknown for unavailable historical times and give the extension its own three full lifecycle datetimes with time and timezone.
scenarios.must_not: Fabricate historical times, reuse the parent approval time, or use date-only extension timestamps.

feedback.trigger: The task router runs in a Codex session after repository-owned telemetry was retired.
feedback.actual_behavior: The skill instructs Codex to emit a CODEX_SKILL_RUN marker as a telemetry side effect.
feedback.expected_behavior: Route the request without emitting telemetry markers or interacting with telemetry hooks.
feedback.invariant: Task routing has no telemetry side effect.

scenarios.request: Route a docs-only request into the correct workflow branch.
scenarios.context: The repository retired its telemetry flow and global hook templates.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Select the docs-only branch and continue without emitting a telemetry marker.
scenarios.must_not: Emit CODEX_SKILL_RUN or start a telemetry lifecycle.

scenarios.request: Route a code change that needs an approved SOW.
scenarios.context: The request must still follow normal SOW-first routing.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Require or find the approved SOW, then hand off to execution without telemetry output.
scenarios.must_not: Change SOW routing because telemetry is unavailable.

scenarios.request: Route work in a project that independently operates telemetry.
scenarios.context: That project's telemetry ownership is external to this skill.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Route only the task and leave telemetry ownership to the external project workflow.
scenarios.must_not: Emit, configure, or manage telemetry hooks.

feedback.trigger: Routing a narrow request reveals analogous or adjacent surfaces.
feedback.actual_behavior: The router pressures every request toward family-level scope and labels a narrow request as a trade-off.
feedback.expected_behavior: Inspect adjacent impact without adding repair scope unless it is necessary and already authorized.
feedback.invariant: Adjacent inspection informs scope but does not create implementation authority.

scenarios.request: Fix one bounded caller that violates an established contract.
scenarios.context: A cheap search finds similar callers, but no evidence shows they share the defect.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Keep the approved fix narrow and report other callers only if useful for later investigation.
scenarios.must_not: Require a family-wide repair or invent a trade-off for honoring the requested scope.

scenarios.request: Repair a shared helper defect affecting all known callers.
scenarios.context: The shared owner is in scope and evidence proves the same defect across callers.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Route the shared in-scope repair and verify affected callers proportionally.
scenarios.must_not: Use bounded scope to force duplicate single-caller patches.

scenarios.request: Fix one caller while proposing a broader compatibility layer.
scenarios.context: The layer may help future callers but is not required or approved for the current outcome.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Route the caller fix and keep the compatibility layer as a separate proposal.
scenarios.must_not: Treat the suggestion as part of approved implementation scope.

feedback.actual_behavior: Debug routing gates only big fixes and docs always wait for approval.
feedback.expected_behavior: Apply target policy and existing authorization regardless of patch size.
feedback.invariant: Apply target policy and existing authorization regardless of patch size.

scenarios.request: Fix this one-line bug.
scenarios.context: The repo requires approved SOWs for all code changes; none covers this bug.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Investigate then draft scope before code edits.
scenarios.must_not: Treat small size as an exemption.

scenarios.request: Correct this typo in the docs now.
scenarios.context: The exact docs correction is already requested; policy permits direct docs edits.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Proceed with the authorized correction.
scenarios.must_not: Ask for the same approval again.

scenarios.request: While fixing the typo, redesign the module.
scenarios.context: Only the docs correction is authorized.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Route the new implementation scope for approval.
scenarios.must_not: Expand the docs authorization to code.

feedback.actual_behavior: The entrypoint references an external repository rule file absent from skill-only installs.

scenarios.request: Route an authorized docs edit.
scenarios.context: Only this skill was copied into a fresh skills root.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Route using packaged instructions.
scenarios.must_not: Read an absent external rule.

scenarios.request: Use the installed router.
scenarios.context: No historical rules folder exists.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Continue without installing policy files.
scenarios.must_not: Require legacy machine setup.

scenarios.request: Use this skill in another agent directory.
scenarios.context: Its skill root is arbitrary and project policy is separate.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Resolve local references within the installed skill.
scenarios.must_not: Create or overwrite project policies.

feedback.trigger: Route a request that explicitly names Claude Code as delegate.
feedback.actual_behavior: The router invents a second provider contract or silently chooses Claude when no transport was requested.
feedback.expected_behavior: Route explicit Claude delegation to sow-delegate-flow and leave model/transport selection unchanged otherwise.
feedback.invariant: Routing selects the single delegate owner without silently changing model authority or creating duplicate transport policy.

scenarios.request: Delegate this approved review to Claude Code.
scenarios.context: The user explicitly names Claude and the target scope is clear.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Route to sow-delegate-flow for its opus/sonnet and session contract.
scenarios.must_not: Create a second Claude CLI syntax in the router.

scenarios.request: Route an ordinary task without naming a model or transport.
scenarios.context: Existing native model-selection and execution policy applies.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use normal routing and do not select Claude solely because the CLI exists.
scenarios.must_not: Turn a model mention in background context into a delegation request.

scenarios.request: Route explicit Claude delegation when the requested CLI/model is unavailable.
scenarios.context: The transport check returns a concrete availability failure.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Return the failure to the delegate flow for its stop/fallback policy; do not invent another route.
scenarios.must_not: Silently substitute a different model, old session, or local implementation.
